A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work and contain complete, readable main text and Appendices A-C. Text, equations, algorithms, and all nine figures support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original random-reward training experiments across Qwen-Math, Llama, and QwQ models, additional analyses in Appendix B, and entropy simulations in Figure 9.

after.justification: v3 retains these original training experiments, appendix analyses, and entropy simulations.

M1.justification: The GRPO procedures, softmax policy update, clipping, and Bernoulli random rewards are unchanged. Algorithm 1 is relocated without changing its steps; the revised entropy analysis does not introduce a training-method change.

E1.justification: Both versions use DeepScaleR and harder AIME training data, MATH500 validation, and the same two-action entropy simulations. No dataset, task, or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: The corresponding clipped-versus-unclipped training comparisons and base-versus-trained model comparisons are retained. No evaluated comparator is added, removed, or replaced.

E3.justification: Training and evaluation settings remain unchanged, including batch size 128, default group size 16, learning rate 5e-7, rollout-length configurations, and the clipping/group-size ablation settings. Revised thresholds in Appendix C.3 belong to the mathematical argument.

E4.justification: The clipping-threshold and group-size ablations, harder-data cases, policy-skewness analysis, and entropy simulations are retained with the same evidence in Figures 5-9.

E5.justification: Six-run reporting in Figures 4-5, ten simulation trials in Figure 9, error bars, and raw-versus-smoothed trajectory conventions are unchanged.

E6.justification: Experimental plots and scores are unchanged. The theoretical numerical illustration is recalculated: v1 Remark C.4 reports Phi_min = -2.23e-6 and clipping correction -6.72e-8; v3 Remark C.7 reports -2.23e6 and -2.01e-7, respectively, and an explicit final expected entropy-change bound below -1.49e-7.

T1.justification: Appendix C.3 substantially revises the entropy proof. v3 introduces an envelope-dependent remainder bound and conditional corollary, reorganizes existing moment calculations, and replaces v1's support/minimum-probability argument with the low-probability collision bound in Lemma C.6. Theorem 4.3 now uses the unclipped expansion's remainder R(eta) instead of R_c(eta), with a revised numerical verification.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central claims about clipping, entropy, and model-dependent benefits of spurious rewards. Revised proofs support those retained claims without redefining the contributions.

C2.justification: Appendix C.3 removes v1's assertion that remainder tightening cannot benefit the unclipped setting but becomes useful with upper clipping. v3 instead presents a general conditional bound applied to the common remainder. The broader interpretations of performance, stability, and contamination are retained.

D1.justification: The verl framework, boxed-answer prompting, hyperparameter disclosures, rollout lengths, and sampling details remain unchanged. No implementation or resource-access information is added or removed.

R1.justification: The cited works, reference list, and research positioning in Appendix A remain unchanged. Citation-format edits do not change the relationship to prior research.

P1.justification: v3 updates the title spelling and publication header, names Theorem 3.4 'Law of Clipping,' and edits cross-references. Appendix C.3 receives localized rewriting and reorganization into separate lemmas and a corollary; the overall narrative structure is retained.

P2.justification: All nine figure graphics are unchanged. Algorithm 1 moves from page 22 to page 21, Figure 9 moves from page 29 to page 30, and revised equation displays alter appendix pagination and spacing.

improvement.justification: v3 makes the entropy remainder argument more explicit and organized, replaces the clipped-support construction, and repairs numerical inconsistencies and a broken reference in the practical entropy-decrease example. These are useful gains in mathematical transparency and checkability, while the experimental evidence and headline conclusions remain unchanged.
